page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.xlarge is an ARM64-based compute-optimized server powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at 2.5 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It includes a bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The Nitro hypervisor manages the virtualization layer.

Benchmark results indicate average performance in several areas, alongside notable limitations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scored 1519.58 and 6061.97 respectively, placing them in the average category. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also average, with read-only speeds at 72.54 GB/sec and write speeds at 33.66 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is weak at 235.91 GB/sec. The server exhibits poor performance in Geekbench single-core (932.0) and Passmark CPU (2694.32) tests. Cryptographic capabilities are supported via AES hardware instructions, though the Passmark CPU encryption test scored a poor 540.75.

The c6gd.xlarge presents a tradeoff between dedicated compute cores with local NVMe storage and lower memory-to-CPU ratios. It lacks advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX, AVX512, and AMX. This hardware profile is suited for workloads that require dedicated ARM64 compute resources and local high-speed scratch storage, such as database operations, where it achieved an average Passmark database score of 2607.7. It is less suited for memory-intensive applications, heavy text processing, or large language model inference, where benchmarks show poor to weak performance.
